narr: An active weather pattern, combined with excessive atmospheric moisture, produced numerous showers and thunderstorms October 4th and early October 5th. Heavy rainfall amounts of 3 to 5 inches were common over central Georgia, with higher amounts up to 10 inches in and around Columbus and West Point in west central Georgia. Isolated flash flooding was also reported around Gainesville, resulting from 2.5 to 4 inches of rainfall.
ev: The Emergency Manager reported that River Road near Green Island Hills was closed due to flooding. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 5 inches of rain occurred over the area at the time of the report, with a total of 6 to 10 inches estimated for the day.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding of I-185 at Williams Road. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 5 inches of rain occurred over the area at the time of the report, with a total of 6 to 10 inches estimated for the day.

Broadcast Media reported floodwaters from Bull Creek was surrounding numerous apartments homes with a few inches of water. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 5 inches of rain occurred over the area at the time of the report, with a total of 6 to 10 inches estimated for the day.

The Emergency Manager and local Broadcast Media reported floodwaters from Weracoba Creek had inundated Lakebottom Park. Radar estimates indicate that a daily-total of 6 to 10 inches accumulated in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

Broadcast Media reported approximately one foot of water flowing over Cusseta Road near Brown Avenue, associated with high flow from Weracoba Creek. Radar estimates indicate that a daily-total of 6 to 10 inches accumulated in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding at several locations in Gainesville, including but not limited to Chestatee Road at Pearl Nix Parkway, 1300 block of Cumberland Drive, 1700 block of MLK Boulevard, Wessell Road at Dixon Drive, High Street at Pine Street, and Race Street between Jesse Jewell Parkway and College Avenue. Radar estimates indicate that a 2.5 to 3 inches accumulated in the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager relayed a report of flood waters over Gay Road from Blackwell Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 4.5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported Shepherd Road closed due to flooding from Sheppard Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 4.5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
